summary.text: Lou Correa is the Democratic incumbent in the 46th District, which covers Orange County cities including Anaheim and Santa Ana, and has served in the U.S. House since he was elected in 2016.

Before Congress he held office in the California State Assembly, on the Orange County Board of Supervisors and in the California State Senate; his campaign website describes him as the son of working-class parents who has served Orange County since 1998.

paragraphs.text: Correa was born in East Los Angeles, and after his mother's death the family spent several years in Zacatecas, Mexico, before he and his father settled in the Penguin City neighborhood of Anaheim, where he began second grade speaking only Spanish.

His official biography says his mother cleaned hotel rooms across from Disneyland and his father worked at a paper mill, and that he attended Benjamin Franklin Elementary, Fremont Junior High and Anaheim High School.
He earned a B.A. in economics from California State University, Fullerton in 1980, and an MBA and Juris Doctor from UCLA in 1985.
He worked as a teacher in the Rancho Santiago Community College District and as an investment banker, attorney and licensed real estate broker.

Correa lost a 1996 race for the California State Assembly to the Republican incumbent by 93 votes, then won the seat in a 1998 rematch; he served in the Assembly from 1998 to 2004, chairing the Business and Professions Committee and the Public Employees, Retirement and Social Security Committee among others, until term limits ended his service.

He was elected to the Orange County Board of Supervisors in 2004, becoming the first Democrat on the board since 1987, and represented the first supervisorial district, which includes Garden Grove, Santa Ana and Westminster, until 2006.

He then served in the California State Senate from 2006 to 2014, winning the 34th District seat in 2006 and re-election in 2010; in a January 2015 special election he lost a race for the Orange County Board of Supervisors by 43 votes.

Correa won the 46th District seat in 2016 after Rep. Loretta Sanchez left it to run for U.S. Senate; he finished first in the June top-two primary and defeated fellow Democrat Bao Nguyen in the general election with about 70% of the vote.

For 2025 and 2026 he is assigned to the House Homeland Security Committee, where he is ranking member of the Subcommittee on Border Security and Enforcement, and to the Judiciary Committee; he is a member of the New Democrat Coalition and the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.
In July 2024 he was named one of six Democratic members of a bipartisan House task force investigating the attempted assassination of Donald Trump.
Correa lives in Santa Ana with his wife, Esther, and their four children, and is a member of Christ Cathedral Catholic Church, according to his official biography.
